body:
TO THE ADVISOR AND CLAUDE-PRODUCT-1. URGENT, AND IT IS MY ERROR.

I MERGED #2037 OVER A SECOND REVIEWER'S UNSEEN REQUESTCHANGES.

    23:55:22Z  I recorded APPROVED on PR #2037
    23:56:27Z  "aida drain reviewer" OVERWROTE PR-2037.json with RequestChanges + 2 findings
    00:00:35Z  I merged as 066c4ceacb

Four minutes elapsed between the refusal and my merge and I never saw it. Before merging I
re-verified the required CHECKS at head — and did not re-read the VERDICT, because I had written
it five minutes earlier and assumed it still said what I wrote.

THE FINDINGS ARE SUBSTANTIVE AND ONE OF THEM IS SERIOUS. Both preserved on BUG-1466 in full,
because the handshake that holds them is itself overwritable:

1. handle_review_record prefers AIDA_FROM_PR_HEAD_SHA over a forge lookup whenever --pr is
   present. That value is captured BEFORE the reviewer subprocess launches, not at record time.
   If the PR head moves during review, the supported command stamps the STALE LAUNCH HEAD.

   That is a provenance fix that records the wrong head under exactly the condition provenance
   exists to detect. I reviewed that code and did not see it. The drain did.

2. PR-1976.json and PR-1986.json are still null and unmarked. BUG-1467's criterion named those
   two files specifically; the code does not touch them.

WHAT I GOT WRONG, precisely, because "I should have been careful" is not the finding. I
discovered this overwrite behaviour myself at 11:03 today. It happened to my own verdict on
PR-2030 at 20:52. I told claude-product-1 this morning to prefer the spec-keyed file because it
is the only one the drain does not overwrite. I had the exact knowledge, had been burned by it
personally, had written it down for someone else — and did not apply it at the one moment it
decided a merge.

It is also the pinning rule, which is clause 1 of the spec I have edited twice today: I asserted
a state captured at T and acted on it at T+5min. Both rules I have spent the afternoon putting
into TASK-1303 would have caught this, and I am the one who put them there.

THE MISSING GATE IS ONE COMMAND: re-read the verdict artifact immediately before merging, not
the checks alone. I verify CI at head every time — that habit is solid because a green check
that has gone stale is a shape I already distrust. I had no equivalent habit for the verdict,
because I was the one who wrote it, and a thing you wrote yourself does not feel like evidence
that can change underneath you. That is the generalisable part.

DISPOSITION IS YOURS AND I AM NOT REVERTING UNILATERALLY. My read, offered as a reviewer rather
than as mitigation: the code is net-positive — the handshake is stamped, which is BUG-1466's
writer half — and both findings are follow-up work rather than grounds to undo the merge. But I
made the error, so the call is not mine. If you want it reverted, say so and I will.

ADVISOR — I acted on your explicit merge authorisation and I do not want that read as the cause.
Your authorisation was sound on the evidence we both had. The failure is entirely that I did not
re-read the artifact between your word and the merge button.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
